1.1  CCEA Approved MSP hike for all Rabi crops for 2027-28 season; MSP procurement of pulses and oilseeds in 3 Statesp.6
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval of MSP Hike for rabi crops
  • Approved by: CCEA, chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Marketing Season: 2027-28
  • Expected Margin: Ranges from 50% to 106% (over the All-India weighted average cost of production)
  • Highest Increase: Safflower at Rs 675 per quintal (+10.3%)
  • Other Key Approval: Procurement of oilseeds and pulses at MSP
  • Total Cost: Rs 5,547.99 crore
  • Season: Kharif Marketing Season (2026-27)
  • Procurement under scheme: PSS
  • Procurement in States: 03, including UP, Karnataka and Telangana
MSP for Rabi Crops for 2027-28 Season:
  • Highest MSP: The highest absolute increase approved for safflower by Rs 675 to Rs 7,215 per quintal, followed by rapeseed & mustard by Rs 413 to Rs 6,613 and lentil (masur) by Rs 390 to Rs 7,390 per quintal.
  • MSP for wheat & Barley: MSP for wheat was increased by Rs 25 to Rs 2,610 per quintal, while barley MSP was increased by Rs 136 to Rs 2,286 per quintal.
  • Increase in Cost of Production: The estimated cost of production for wheat is Rs 1,264 per quintal, providing the highest margin of 106%, while barley has a cost of Rs 1,447 with a 58% margin.Other estimated costs and margins are Gram – Rs 3,751 (59%), Lentil – Rs 3,854 (92%), Rapeseed & Mustard – Rs 3,367 (96%), and Safflower – Rs 4,810 (50%).
Increase in Procurement & MSP Payments:
  • Procurement: Wheat procurement increased from 2,254 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14 to 3,715 LMT during 2014-15 to 2025-26.Cumulative procurement of the six Rabi crops increased from 2,302 LMT to 3,921 LMT during the corresponding periods.

1.4  Cabinet Approves Rs 53,428 Crore for Continuation of the NSAP for 5 yearsp.10
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval for the continuation of NSAP
  • Approved by: Union Cabinet, chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Extended Time Period: From FY27 to FY31
  • Total Budget Approved: Rs 53,428 crore
  • NSAP Renamed to: Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana
  • Renamed 4 Sub-schemes of NSAP: Old-age Pension: from IGNOAPS to Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension YojanaWidow Pension: IGNWP to Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana.Disability Pension: IGNDPS changed to Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana;Family: National Family Benefit scheme changed to Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana
  • Changes under Disability Scheme: Monthly Financial Assistance: Rs 375 (aged up to 79 years); Rs 625 (aged 80 and above)Reduction in Disability Threshold: from 80% to 40%Waived Off Minimum Age Requirement: Starting from birth.Other Approval: Railway PLB -78 Days’ Wages; Rs 2,009.61 Cr.
About National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP):
  • Launch: The scheme was launched on August 15 1995, the programme was designed for assistance to poor households aligned with the Directive Principles of State Policy in Article 41 of the Constitution of India.
Key Changes:
  • Changes under Disability Scheme: The cabinet has raised the monthly financial assistance to Rs 375 for beneficiaries aged up to 79 and Rs 625 for those aged 80 and above.Also, the qualifying benchmark disability threshold reduced from the existing 80% to 40%, aligning with the Rights of Persons with Disability Act 2016 which has mandated the disability related assistance to be invariably 25% higher than similarly placed schemes for other categories.Under the revised minimum-age criterion, eligibility for the scheme will now start from birth.
Cabinet Approves 78-Day Productivity-Linked Bonus for Railway Employees:
  • Union Cabinet has approved a Productivity-Linked Bonus (PLB) equivalent to 78 days’ wages for around 11.4 lakh non-gazetted employees.The approved bonus will incur an expenditure of nearly Rs 2,009.61 crore to the Railways.

1.5  Union Cabinet Approves Rs. 10,000 Crore CMPS to Establish Global Container Manufacturing Ecosystem in Indiap.12
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval of Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS).
  • Approved by: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi.
  • Total outlay: Rs. 10,000 crore.
  • Announced in: Union Budget 2026–27.
  • Implementation period: FY28 to FY40
  • Target capacity: 7.5 lakh TEUs annually
  • Key components: ISA, OEA, Testing and Certification Assistance, Land Leasing Support and Scheme Management
  • Expected economic output: Around Rs. 75,000 crore by FY 2039–40.
  • Local-content requirement: 70% until FY32, increasing to 90% from FY33.
  • Other Approvals: 3% hike in DA & DR
  • Revised rate: 63%, increased from 60%.
Background:
  • The scheme will run from Financial Year 2027–2028 (FY28) to (FY40), comprising three years for setting up manufacturing facilities and ten years of production support.
About Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme:
  • Objective: CMPS will increase India’s annual container manufacturing capacity from approximately 70,000 to 7.5 lakh Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU), generating an estimated Rs. 75,000 crore in economic output by FY40, over seven times the government support.
Components of CMPS:
  • Operational Expenditure Assistance (OEA): With an allocation of Rs. 8,891 crore, OEA supports eligible containers manufactured to global shipping standards and sold by approved manufacturers with minimum local-content requirements of 70% until FY32 and 90% from FY33.It offers Rs. 49,500 per standard 20-ft container, Rs. 86,625 per standard 40-ft container, and Rs. 37,125–Rs. 74,250 per specialised 20-ft container.
About Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW):
  • Union Minister: Sarbananda Sonowal (Constituency- Dibrugarh, Assam) Minister of State (MoS)- Shantanu Thakur (Constituency- Bangaon, West Bengal, WB)

1.9  Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla & Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan Reconstituted 24 DRSCsp.17
Exam Hints:
  • What: Reconstitution of 24 DRSCs
  • Reconstituted by: Om Birla, Speaker of Lok Sabha and CP Radhakrishnan
  • Term: 2026-27
  • Effective From: September 26, 2027
  • Heads of Key Committees: Committee on Finance: Bhartruhari Mahtab (BJP MP)Committee on External Affairs: Shashi Tharoor
Background:
  • As per the official notification, the term of these committees will be effective from September 26, 2026.
Key Details of the Composition:
  • Committee on Finance: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Member of Parliament (MP) Bhartruhari Mahtab appointed chairperson of the committee on Finance that includes 21 members from Lok Sabha and 10 members from Rajya Sabha.
  • Committee on External Affairs: It will be headed by Congress MP Shashi Tharoor. The committee comprises 21 members from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha.
About Departmentally-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs):
  • Constitution of DRSCs: Based on the recommendation of the Rules Committee of the Lok Sabha, 17 DRSCs were originally constituted in the Parliament in 1993. Later, 7 more such committees were formed in 2004, thus increasing the total strength of such committees from 17 to 24.
  • Composition: Each standing committee consists of 31 members i.e. 21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha.
  • Distribution of DRSCs: Out of the 24 DRSCs, 8 work under the Rajya Sabha Chairman and remaining 16 under the Lok Sabha Speaker.

1.11  Union Minister Bhupender Yadav Launches India’s First PRAMAAN Forest Certificationp.20
Exam Hints:
  • What: Launch of India’s First PRAMAAN Certification under IFWCS
  • By Whom: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, MoEFCC
  • When: 29 September 2026
  • Where: New Delhi
  • Recipients: APFDC & Govind Mohapatra (Bamboo Farmer)
  • Implemented by: IIFM, Bhopal, MP
Highlights of PRAMAAN Certificates:
  • First Certification Rollout: India issued its first PRAMAAN certificates, marking the shift from policy framework to on-ground implementation in forest and agroforestry certification.
  • Beneficiaries: Certificates were awarded to the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC) for plantations covering 33,000 hectares, and to Govind Mohapatra, a bamboo farmer associated with the Odisha Bamboo Development Agency (OBDA).
  • Framework: PRAMAAN covers Forest Management (FM), Trees Outside Forests (TOF), and Chain of Custody (CoC), ensuring traceability of forest and non-timber forest products across supply chains.
  • Accreditation system: Certification is based on independent third-party audits (not self-declaration), aligned with the National Working Plan Code (NWPC) 2023, and accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) under the Quality Council of India (QCI).It Supports deforestation-free sourcing, boosts market access, and promotes livelihoods.

India’s TB Elimination Progress:
  • TB Mukt Panchayats: A total of 67,933 Panchayats across 697 districts were recognised as TB Mukt (TB-free) in 2026.The intensified TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched in December 2024 to strengthen early detection, diagnosis and treatment of TB.
  • TB Incidence: India recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence, compared with the global decline of 12%, while its TB treatment coverage rose to 92%, exceeding the global coverage of 78%.
About Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (PMTBMBA):
  • Overview: Launched on 9 September 2022 by President Droupadi Murmu, the nationwide initiative aims to achieve a TB-free India ahead of global Sustainable Development Goal (SDG Target 3.3) 2030 target.

Key Details of Revised CAFE Norms:
  • Fuel Consumption Target: Under the new CAFE framework, the fuel-consumption benchmark will be tightened progressively from 3.996 litres(l)/100 kilometre (km) (in 2027–28) to 3.3273 litres/100 km (2031–32), representing an improvement of nearly 16.7% over a period of 5 years.
  • Revised Vehicle Weights: Also, the Government of India (GoI) has raised the reference vehicle weight from 1,082 kilogram (kg) to 1,229 kg.
  • Compliance Credits & Accumulate Debits: As per the new rules, manufacturers who exceed their prescribed targets will generate compliance credits, while those failing to achieve their targets will accumulate debits.So in order to offset a debit balance, manufacturers can buy credit from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) and will increase from Rs 2,500 per g CO2/km (in 2027-28) to Rs 4,500 per g CO2/km (in 2031-32).These credits received will be calculated by Rule 8 of the Energy Conservation (Compliance Enforcement) Rules, 2025.

About Classical Languages of India:
  • Background: In 2004, the Government of India (GoI) introduced a new category of languages “classical languages”.Between 2004 to 2014, 6 Indian languages namely, Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Kannada (2008), Telugu (2008), Malayalam (2013), and Odia (2014), were conferred the status of classical languages.
  • Expansion: On October 3, 2024, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the inclusion of 5 more Indian languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali to this category, thereby expanding the recognised Classical Languages to 11.
  • Criteria: Classical Language status is based on 1,500–2,000 years of antiquity, a rich body of ancient heritage literature, and an independent tradition of knowledge texts, prose, poetry, epigraphical and inscriptional evidence not borrowed from another speech community.

About Principal Purpose Test (PPT):
  • PPT: The provision allows tax treaty benefits to be denied if obtaining those benefits was one of the principal purposes of a transaction or arrangement, unless granting them is consistent with the object and purpose of the relevant treaty provisions.
  • Treaty Amendment: India and Mauritius signed the protocol on March 7, 2024, in Port Louis, Mauritius; the amended treaty came into force on August 10, 2026, and was notified in India on October 13, 2026.
  • Protection: Pre-April 1, 2017, investments are exempt from PPT, while Mauritius-based investors and funds may face greater scrutiny.
  • Impact on Investors: Mauritius-based investors and investment funds claiming treaty benefits may face greater scrutiny regarding the commercial substance and purpose of their transactions.

  • Phase-wise Implementation: For the initial phase, the framework targets to cover larger societies exceeding the Rs 1,000 crore (nearly USD 120 million) threshold and subsequently, plans to extend the framework to societies surpassing the prescribed threshold of Rs 50 crore (nearly USD 6 million) in relevant financial parameters.

Key Details:
  • Timeline: Phase 1 will begin in for April 2029 new cars and SUVs, Phase 2 in April 2031 will introduce initial brake-wear and tyre-emission limits, and Phase 3 in April 2035 will introduce common, stricter brake-particle and particle-mass limits across all powertrains.Also, the MoRTH has clarified that the timeline for two-wheelers will be notified later.
  • Emission Limit: Though the proposed thresholds for most emission component cards and SUVs remain unchanged from BS-VI (which are in force since April 2020), the Government of India (GoI) has reduced the permitted particulate matter from 23 nanometres (nm) to 10 nm.
  • Other Key Directions: As per the new norms, electric cars and plug-in hybrids are required to retain minimum 75% of initial battery capacity after 5 years or 100, 000 km; and 67% after 8 years or 1, 60, 000 km, whichever comes 1st.

6.9  SEBI Issues Circular Revising Closing Auction Session Framework in Equity Cash Segment; Effective December 7, 2026p.140
Exam Hints:
  • What: SEBI overhauls CAS Framework in equity cash market segment
  • Implementation: December 7, 2026
  • Separate session: 3.30 PM to 3.40 PM
  • Three sessions: 3.30 PM to 3.31 PM, 3.31 PM to 3.36 PM, 3.36 PM to 3.40 PM
  • Closing: 3.38 PM to 3.40 PM
  • Reference Price: Calculated based on VWAP
  • Index Derivative: 3.45 PM on regular days, 3.30 PM on expiry days
  • Stock derivative: 3.45 PM on all days
  • Unexecuted Orders: From CTS into CAS.
Background:
  • The revised framework shall come into effect from December 07, 2026.
CAS Framework Overhaul Details:
  • CAS: dedicated stock exchange mechanism introduced by SEBI in India in August, 2026, to determine the official closing price of eligible equity shares.
  • Separate session: CAS shall be implemented as a separate session of 10 minutes from 3:30 PM to 3.40 PM on all trading days.It currently runs from 3:15 PM to 3:35 PM.
  • Three sessions: The new session has three phases:Phase 1 (3.30 PM to 3.31 PM): The reference price is calculated and trading moves from the Continuous Trading Session (CTS) to CAS.Phase 2 (3.31 PM to 3.36 PM): Limit and market orders can be placed.Phase 3 (3.36 PM to 3.40 PM): Only limit orders can be placed, and market orders cannot be modified or cancelled.
  • Closing: The order entry session shall close randomly anytime between 3:38 PM to 3:40 PM.
  • Post-Closing Session: The equity cash market’s post-closing session will operate from 3:50 PM to 4:00 PM, with trades executed at the closing price.

  • Penalty: Rs 10,000
  • Show cause notice: Rs 10,000
  • Capital goods: 60month ITC refund from April 2027

  • Rule 14B: Council recommended introducing Rule 14B under the CGST Rules, 2017, to facilitate registration for small suppliers selling goods through e-commerce operators in States or Union Territories (UTs) where they have no physical presence.
  • Penalty: The general penalty was reduced from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000.For eligible non-fraud cases, the penalty was proposed to be reduced to 5%, provided the tax and interest were paid within 30 days under Section 73 or 60 days under Section 74A from the date of the order.
  • Show-cause notice: Show-cause notices were not to be issued for tax amounts below Rs 10,000.The same threshold was proposed to apply to pending notices and appeals involving amounts below Rs 10,000.
Input Tax Credit (ITC) Reforms:
  • Capital Goods: Refunds of eligible ITC on capital goods used for zero-rated supplies and under the inverted duty structure were approved, to be disbursed over 60 months for credit availed from April 1, 2027.

15.3  QNu Labs & BISAG-N Demonstrate India’s First 5.56 km Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution Linkp.288
Exam Hints:
  • What: Demonstration of India’s First free-space QKD link
  • By whom: QNu Labs, BISAG-N, IIT Gandhinagar
  • Distance: 5.56 km
  • Date of Demo: September 27–28, 2026
  • Software Used: BISAG-N’s Vedic Kavach platform
  • Hardware Used: QNu Labs’ Armos QKD device & PAT system
  • Significance: Step towards quantum-secure and satellite communication systems
Background:
  • The field trial was conducted on September 27–28, 2026, establishing a secure quantum communication link between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar, Gujarat.
Highlights of India’s First Free-Space QKD Demonstration:
  • Technology: Utilised Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking (PAT) system to achieve stable communication with a Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) below 5% and generated secure encryption keys at 230–260 bits per second (bps).
  • Integration: The generated keys were integrated with Vedic Kavach platform, enabling end-to-end encryption and decryption, while combining hardware-based QKD using Armos device and software-based post-quantum cryptography.
  • Security: The system operates on a dual-layer security architecture, combining the Armos QKD device and Vedic Kavach, ensuring secure communication even if the quantum channel is disrupted.
  • Significance: India’s first 5.56 km free-space QKD demonstration, enabling future long-distance and satellite-based quantum communication and strengthening secure communication against quantum threats.

Background:

About Kaveri Dry Engine (KDE):
  • Background: Initiated in 1986 and sanctioned in 1989 for Light Combat Aircraft (LCA)Tejas, it aimed to develop a low-bypass turbofan with afterburner, but was not inducted due to thrust-to-weight and weight limitations, and was later adapted into the KDE without an afterburner
  • High-Altitude Testing: The engine was evaluated at CIAM under simulated high-altitude conditions to assess its performance across varying pressure and temperature environments.
  • Flight Testing: Flight evaluations at the Gromov Flight Research Institute recorded a maximum dry thrust of 48.5 kilonewtons (kN), surpassing the target of 46 kN.
About Ghatak Stealth UCAV:
  • Design: Ghatak UCAV is built using 80–90% carbon-fibre composites (CFC) for reduced weight and enhanced performance, and features a tailless flying-wing design with stealth elements such as curved air intakes and shaped exhaust systems.

About the 1962 Sino-Indian War:
  • Conflict Regions: The war between India and China was fought along disputed Himalayan borders, particularly in Aksai Chin (Ladakh) and the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA, present-day Arunachal Pradesh).
  • Ceasefire: China announced a unilateral ceasefire on 20 November 1962, effective from 21 November, and subsequently withdrew from certain occupied areas, while retaining control of Aksai Chin.
  • War Outcome: India suffered a military defeat, with thousands of soldiers killed, wounded or captured, while China consolidated its control over Aksai Chin.

  • First Observance: The day was first observed on 21 October 1960, in memory of the police personnel killed in the 1959 incident.
History of the 1959 Incident:
  • CRPF Patrol: On 20 October 1959, three patrol parties of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) were deployed near the India–Tibet border in Ladakh.
  • Search Operation: On 21 October 1959, a search party of 20 police personnel, led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Karam Singh, was attacked by Chinese troops near Hot Springs.
  • Casualties: Ten police personnel were killed, while seven were captured. The bodies of the martyrs were handed over by Chinese authorities on 13 November 1959.

20.58  International Day of Care and Support 2026 – October 29p.397
Exam Hints:
  • What: International Day of Care and Support 2026
  • When: 29 October (4th observance)
  • Observed by: United Nations
  • 2026 Theme: “Building Sustainable Care and Support Systems through Decent Work”
  • Established by: UNGA Resolution A/RES/77/317 (2023)
  • First Observed: 29 October 2023
  • 2026 Event: ILO commemoration in Geneva, Switzerland
Background:
  • 29 October 2026 marks the 4th observance of the IDCS.
Background:
  • Establishment: On 24 July 2023, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) adopted Resolution A/RES/77/317, proclaiming 29 October as the International Day of Care and Support (IDCS).
  • First Observance: The first IDCS was observed on 29 October 2023.
Key Facts:
  • Global Care Workforce: 381 million people work in the care economy worldwide, approximately 65% of whom are women.
  • Global Care Workforce: 249 million women and 132 million men work in the global care workforce (ILO).
  • Unpaid Care Work: Women perform 76.2% of unpaid care work, spending 3.2 times more time on it than men.
  • Care Demand: By 2030, care recipients are projected to reach 2.3 billion worldwide.
  • Employment Projection: Employment in education, health and social work could reach 248 million jobs by 2030.
  • Job Creation: Investment in the care economy could support 475 million jobs by 2030, according to an ILO study.
International Labour Organization (ILO) - Static GK:
Director-General (DG): Gilbert F. Houngbo, the first African to head the ILO
Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
Established: 1919.

  • Web Portal: Village-level ARS zonation maps

  • States/UT with Highest Over-Exploited Groundwater Units: Punjab (75.16%), Haryana (61.54%), Delhi (41.18%), Tamil Nadu (TN) (33.87%) and Karnataka (18.99%).
  • National Water Mission (NWM): It was established in 2011 under the MoJS. It aims to improve water-use efficiency by 20% and reduce over-exploited groundwater blocks by at least 20% by 2035.

22.2  Three New Centipede Species Discovered in Western Ghatsp.405
Exam Hints:
  • What: Three new centipede species discovered
  • Name of Species: Rhysida quadrispinosa, Rhysida coorgensis and Rhysida neyyarensis
  • Location: Western Ghats, Kerala and Karnataka
  • Research Institutions: ZSI’s Western Ghats Regional Centre and Malabar Christian College, Kozhikode
  • Published In: International Journal of Tropical Insect Science
  • Genus: Rhysida
  • Total Known Rhysida Species: 23
Background:
  • The findings, published in the International Journal of Tropical Insect Science, increased the number of known Rhysida species in India to 23.
About Newly Discovered Species:
  • Rhysida quadrispinosa: Named for four distinctive spines on its ultimate-leg prefemur; it has 18 antennal segments and distinctive body margins and hind-leg spine arrangements.
  • Rhysida coorgensis: Named after Coorg, Karnataka, where it was collected; distinguished by back-plate markings and spine arrangements.
  • Rhysida neyyarensis: Named after Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary, Kerala; identified by two tarsal spurs on each of its first 19 leg pairs.
  • About ZSI: Established in 1916 and headquartered in Kolkata, West Bengal, the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) conducts research, surveys and documentation of India’s faunal diversity.

22.3  Ghostly Eyeless Freshwater Snail Discovered in China’s Yunnan Provincep.405
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of Erhaia dijiang, an eyeless freshwater cave snail.
  • Where: Mountain cave, Yuxi City, Yunnan Province, China.
  • Elevation: 2,062 m above sea level.
  • Journal: Subterranean Biology.
  • Family: Erhaiidae.
Background:
  • Findings Were Published in Subterranean Biology, the discovery raised conservation concerns as only three living adults were found.
About the New Creature:
  • Adaptation: Erhaia dijiang has lost its eyes and body pigmentation, with a nearly transparent, cone-shaped shell and long, slender tentacles that reflect its adaptation to underground life.
  • Naming: The species was named after Di Jiang, a faceless mythical creature described in the ancient Chinese text Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shan Hai Jing).
  • Habitat: The snail inhabits shallow cave waters less than one metre deep, among submerged gravel and broken rocks, at a water temperature of approximately 20°C (Celsius).

22.4  Researchers Discover New Flowering Plant Species ‘Osbeckia assamensis’ in Assamp.406
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of New flowering plant species “Osbeckia assamensis”
  • By whom: Prof. Namita Nath, Gauhati University; Barnali Das, Pragjyotish College.
  • Where: Manas National Park, Assam
  • Publication: Peer-reviewed international journal Phytotaxa.
  • Family: Melastomataceae
  • Other Discovery: New giant waterlily species Victoria colombiana
  • Where? Inírida region, Guainía, Colombia
  • Publication: Botanical journal Phytotaxa
  • Taxonomy: Belongs to the genus Victoria and family Nymphaeaceae
About Osbeckia assamensis:
  • Taxonomy: Belongs to the family Melastomataceae and genus Osbeckia, which has 45 accepted species and 6 varieties according to the cited botanical sources.
  • Morphology: A perennial shrub growing 2–2.5 metres (m) tall, with a largely unbranched stem, large opposite leaves and pink flowers measuring 3–3.5 Centimeter (cm).
  • Features: Bears 30–35 flowers per inflorescence, compared with 5–12 in Osbeckia nayarii, and has distinctive stem, leaf, calyx and seed characteristics.
Discovery of Fourth Giant Waterlily Species ‘Victoria colombiana’ in Colombia:
  • In October 2026, scientists formally identified Victoria colombiana, a new giant waterlily species in Colombia’s Inírida region, Guainía, marking the fourth recognised species of the genus Victoria, after Victoria amazonica, Victoria cruziana and Victoria boliviana.The findings were published in the botanical journal Phytotaxa.
  • Conservation: Classified as Critically Endangered, with an estimated 30–50 individual plants remaining in the wild.

22.5  Two New Plant Species Discovered in Arunachal Pradesh’s Changlang Districtp.407
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of two new plant species.
  • Species: Ophiorrhiza shidiensis and Ophiorrhiza pemae.
  • Location: Vijoynagar, Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Family: Rubiaceae (coffee, madder or bedstraw family).
  • Published: 23 October 2026, in the journal Taiwania.
  • Research Institutions: Botanical Survey of India (BSI) and Madras Christian College, Chennai.
Background:
  • Both species belong to the Rubiaceae family, commonly known as the coffee family, and their findings were published on 23 October 2026 in the scientific journal Taiwania.
Highlights of the Discovery:
  • Field Surveys: The researchers first observed the plants during botanical surveys in March 2025 and revisited the sites in April 2026 to collect specimens for detailed examination.
Ophiorrhiza shidiensis:
  • Naming: The species was named after Shidi, the traditional name for Gandhigram used by the Lisu (Yobin) community in AR.
  • Habitat: It grows in damp, shaded forest areas near streams and slopes at elevations of approximately 1,100–2,000 metres(m).
Ophiorrhiza pemae:
  • Naming: The species was named in honour of Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister (CM) Pema Khandu, recognising his contributions to the state’s development and scientific activities.
  • Plant Characteristics: small perennial herb growing approximately 25–40 centimetres tall.
  • Habitat: The species was recorded in temperate montane forests at elevations of approximately 2,100– 2,600 m.

22.6  New Microscopic Land Snail Species Discovered in Kolhapur’s Tilari Regionp.408
Exam Hints:
  • What: New Microscopic land snail Discovered
  • What Species: Dicharax tilariensis.
  • Location: Tilari region, Kolhapur district, Maharashtra.
  • Collection Site: Near Swapnavel Point, close to Tilarinagar.
  • Elevation: 700–800 metres above sea level.
  • Publication: Journal of Conchology, 24 October 2026.
Background:
  • The species is currently known only from this region, making it endemic to the area.
  • The research paper was published in the Journal of Conchology, published by the Conchological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.
About the New Species:
  • Habitat: The snail inhabits microhabitats containing forest litter, decaying organic matter and moist soil in the semi-evergreen forests of Tilari.
  • Naming: The species name Dicharax tilariensis is derived from the Tilari region, its only known habitat.
  • Collection: Specimens were collected near Swapnavel Point, close to Tilarinagar, in Kolhapur district, Maharashtra at an elevation of 700–800 metres (m) above sea level.
  • Identification: Researchers compared its characteristics with other members of the Dicharax genus found across the Western Ghats and southern India.
  • Research Team: The study was conducted by Amrut Bhosale, Tejas Thackeray and Akshay Khandekar of the Thackeray Wildlife Foundation, marking the second Dicharax species endemic to the northern Western Ghats.
